title: Ultralight CMS Package Notes
source: Consolidated package, validation and closure commentary from the CW/UltralightCMS project conversations.

points: Model/model.cw.shards[] is the authoritative canonical Model closure.
Every non-root canonical .cw shard appears exactly once in shards[].
A listed missing shard or an unlisted .cw shard makes the package invalid.
Property identifiers are package-global in the active Model closure and bare Property references resolve by exact id.
A Link is a Property owned by exactly one Entity.
The owner is the declarer of the relation, while parent_ref and child_ref define semantic endpoints independently.
dependency parent_ref is the provider/dependency and child_ref is the dependent/consumer.
dependency is structural and does not imply execution.
Each Entity owns zero or one Asset Property.
The physical Asset filename is derived deterministically from the percent-encoded Entity.id and a registered extension.
The Asset family directory matches the owner Entity family.
The CW package validator checks path, existence, file type, extension and cardinality only.
The validator does not parse payload content, infer payload semantics, MIME-sniff or perform runtime payload schema validation.
An adapter/runtime may decode an Asset and bind resulting values into Data slots, but the non-null binding must satisfy its Schema before becoming READY.
Canonical text is UTF-8 normalized to NFC and canonical paths use slash separators.
Path-bearing fields resolve against explicit bases declared by Format.
Absolute paths, backslashes, empty segments, dot segments and parent traversals are invalid path values.
Case-fold collisions are rejected for portability and symlinks are not canonical package members.
Percent encoding uses UTF-8 bytes and uppercase hexadecimal for every character outside RFC3986 unreserved characters.
CCF version, CW package-format version, Dependency Rules version and modeled-system release version are independent dimensions.
Version sources are referenced rather than duplicated as secondary current values.
CCF 2.4.3 remains unchanged.
The golden remains unlocked until package-aware validation and CIC output converge on the same self-contained structure.
A locked model requires an immutable content-addressed Format closure.
The specification defines the tools; existing tools do not define the specification.
The package-aware linter validates the golden first.
CIC then emits the same package structure and validates its own output against its local Format.
Topology and TUI consume only canonical Model shards plus the separate Format registry and derive views without creating duplicate truth.
